Older names/treatments include Croton capitatus var. genuinus and several generic combinations.

morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Start with the pistillate sepals and leaf tips: long pistillate sepals that flare/recurve outward after anthesis plus at least some blunt or mucronate leaves are strong C. capitatus cues.
diagnostic_traits: stems and leaves densely stellate-hairy with whitish to pale-yellow woolly pubescence
leaves ovate to lanceolate-elliptic; some tips obtuse/rounded or mucronate
pistillate sepals 6–9 and long, persistent, with tips spreading/recurving outward

confusers.separator: C. lindheimeri tends toward ochraceous young pubescence, consistently acute leaf tips, and pistillate sepal tips that stay straight to slightly incurved rather than flaring outward.
C. lindheimerianus is generally a lower, more dichotomously branched annual with smaller pistillate sepals and only six terminal style segments.
